objective: Secure your supply chain: permit only approved registries with admission control (ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or ImagePolicyWebhook), and sign and verify images with cosign
secondaryObjectives: Scan images for known vulnerabilities before deployment and decide what blocks a release
Understand your supply chain: generate and read an SBOM (syft, Trivy), know what CI/CD and artifact repositories introduce, and track image provenance
Minimize the base image footprint with multi-stage builds, distroless or minimal bases, pinned digests and no shells or package managers in the runtime image

The company, the clusters, the workloads and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run platform security at Velora Travel, a fictional booking site. Today's release of the booking service is queued. The cluster admits images from any registry, nothing is signed, and the scanner has just reported a critical vulnerability in the booking image's base layer.
handover: Image: booking:2.14 built FROM a full OS image by tag; Trivy reports one critical CVE in a TLS library with a public exploit, and 41 others.
No admission policy restricts registries; no images are signed; no SBOMs are kept.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: the exploit is used against the booking service's TLS endpoint; session keys leak before the image is replaced.
Check-in 3: a deployment pulls a typo-squatted public image; it mines cryptocurrency with the node's CPU and calls out to an unknown host.
Check-in 4: a new advisory lands for a logging library; with no SBOMs, it takes three days to find the 23 affected images.

effects.log: Check-in 2: time to close the registry gap.
Check-in 3: an auditor asks which images contain a library.

cvePrompt.title: Ship with a critical CVE?
cvePrompt.context: The critical CVE has a public exploit and is reachable (the service terminates TLS). A rebuild takes 20 minutes.

choices.label: Block 2.14, rebuild as a multi-stage image on a patched distroless base pinned by digest, rescan, then release

effects.log: The rebuilt image scans clean of criticals and highs.

choices.feedback: A reachable, exploitable critical blocks a release; the minimal base removes the tools behind the high findings too.

choices.label: Rebuild on the patched full OS base by tag and release

effects.log: The patched full image is released.

choices.feedback: The critical is fixed, but the shell and package manager stay, and a tag can change under you.

choices.label: Ship 2.14 now and patch next sprint
choices.feedback: A public exploit for a reachable critical is not a backlog item.

admitPrompt.title: Images from anywhere
admitPrompt.context: Any image from any registry can run, signed or not.

choices.label: Sign images with cosign in CI; a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy denies images outside the internal registry, and a verification webhook rejects unsigned images; roll out in audit first

effects.log: Registry restriction and signature verification are in audit, then enforced.

choices.feedback: Restricting the registry stops typosquats; verifying signatures proves the image came from your CI.

choices.label: Restrict images to the internal registry, without signatures

effects.log: Only the internal registry is allowed.

choices.feedback: That stops public typosquats, but anyone who can push to the registry can still run anything.

choices.label: Leave admission open and remind developers in the wiki
choices.feedback: A wiki page does not stop a typo in an image name.

sbomPrompt.title: What is inside our images?
sbomPrompt.context: An auditor asks which running images contain the vulnerable TLS library. Nothing records what each image contains.

choices.label: Generate an SBOM with syft in CI for every image and attach it to the image as a signed attestation

effects.log: Every new image carries a signed SBOM.

choices.feedback: An SBOM per image answers 'where is this library?' in minutes, and the attestation ties it to the image.

choices.label: Run a scan across the registry whenever someone asks

effects.log: Ad hoc scans are run when asked.

choices.feedback: It answers eventually, but for images already running nobody can prove what was built.

choices.label: Skip it: the scanner already runs at build time
choices.feedback: A build-time scan answers only for known CVEs at that moment; the next library advisory finds you blind.

reflection.question: Write the release record: why the release was blocked, how admission now controls images, and how you will know what is inside them.

parts.label: Build
parts.criteria: Blocked on the reachable critical; rebuilt multi-stage on a patched distroless base pinned by digest.
parts.modelAnswer: The critical was reachable with a public exploit, so 2.14 was blocked and rebuilt multi-stage on a patched distroless base pinned by digest.

parts.label: Admission and SBOM
parts.criteria: Approved registry plus cosign verification, audited then enforced; a signed SBOM per image.
parts.modelAnswer: Admission allows only signed images from the internal registry; every image carries a signed SBOM.

source.note: Service restored and the work closed within 60 minutes of the first report.

cveHarm.headline: A reachable critical blocks the release
cveHarm.body: Decide what blocks a release before the scan: a reachable critical with a public exploit does.

admitHarm.headline: Admission is the last gate
admitHarm.body: Allow only the approved registry and verify signatures before a Pod runs.

sbomHarm.headline: Know what you run
sbomHarm.body: An SBOM per image, kept with it, answers the next advisory in minutes.

target.headline: Good: a secured supply chain
target.body: Blocked on the critical, minimal and pinned images, signatures and registry enforced at admission, and SBOMs kept.

partly.headline: Done, with gaps
partly.body: Nothing was harmed, but a decision was only partly right, or the record left something out. The criteria say which.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: The record was not written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Decide what blocks a release before scanning: a reachable critical with a public exploit does. Minimal, multi-stage images on a distroless base pinned by digest remove most findings and drift. Admission control is the last gate: allow only the approved registry and verify cosign signatures, rolled out in audit first. An SBOM generated in CI and attached as a signed attestation records what each image contains, so the next advisory is answered in minutes.
